117641.name: Chabad House of Farmington Hills
117641.note: Detroit Jewish News, Nov 24 1972: 'A proud new addition to the multivarious activities of Merkos, BAIS CHABAD is a contemporary Hassidic synagogue and student center in Farmington Township. Housed in a beautiful new building at 28555 Middlebelt Road ... Rabbi Yitschak Kagan heads Bais Chabad together with Rabbi I. M. Lipszyc ... another link in the new network of 71 Lubavitch institutions' the Rebbe asked for in his 71st year; its High Holiday services were there in Aug 1972. It was 'Cong. Bais Chabad of Farmington, Rabbi Y.M. Kagan' in May 1976, and by April 1978 Rabbi Chaim M. Bergstein was 'director of Cong. Bais Chabad of Farmington Hills' (the Bergsteins 'since 1977', Jewish News 2023). So 1972 (corrected from 1977, the Bergsteins' start, after the archive was read again on Nov 7). Where it has been: 28555 Middlebelt Rd. from 1972 (still its address in a Sept 1982 ad); Shabbat services at the Bergsteins' home, 32276 Tareyton, in 1978-81, with High Holidays at 28555 Middlebelt; now 32000 Middlebelt Rd., where lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 already lists it (Rabbi Chaim Bergstein), so it moved there between 1982 and 2009 (https://web.archive.org/web/20091228151704/http://lubavitch.com/centers/list.html?Country=&City=Farmington%20Hills).

earlier.where: 28555 Middlebelt Rd. (the Labor Zionist Institute building, later the Lubavitch Educational Center)
Shabbat services at the Bergsteins' home, 32276 Tareyton

117989.name: Michigan Jewish Institute
117989.note: Founded in 1994, funded by the Lubavitch Foundation of Michigan. CLOSED 2 March 2016 after losing federal aid: the directory listing is out of date. From August 1997 at 25401 Coolidge Hwy., Oak Park (Jewish News: 'Our new address as of August 1997'), still there in 2006 and in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 (Rabbi Kasriel Shemtov), before its West Bloomfield address (6888 Maple Road), so it moved after 2009 (https://web.archive.org/web/20091228163919/http://lubavitch.com/centers/list.html?Country=&City=Oak%20Park).

earlier.where: 25401 Coolidge Hwy., Oak Park (still its address in Dec 2009)

393834.name: Chabad of Novi
393834.note: Jewish News, 12 Jan 2006: 'In the three months since Rabbi Avrohom and Leah Susskind began the Chabad Jewish Center of Novi-Northville...'; before moving from Oak Park they held a first program in Novi, Purim at the Novi Civic Center, March 2005. (Corrected: the July 2024 list says 2000.) lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 1 2011 lists it at 42142 Loganberry Ridge N., Novi; it is now at 40550 Grand River Avenue, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 42142 Loganberry Ridge N., Novi (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 1 2011)

117711.name: Chabad House-Lubavitch of Greater Toledo
117711.note: Rabbi Shemtov and his family brought Chabad House to Toledo in 1987, at first from their home on Secor Road (Toledo Blade, 2018). Checked: listed as Chabad House of Toledo, Rabbi Yosef Y. Shemtov, in May 1987 (Jewish News). Its own building, 2728 King Road, was dedicated in Sept 2018 (Toledo Blade). lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 4020 Nantucket Drive, Toledo (with the Chai Jewish Student Center at 4230 Rose Garden Drive), before its own building at 2728 King Road (2018).

earlier.where: the Shemtovs' home on Secor Road
4020 Nantucket Drive, Toledo (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

117644.name: F.R.E.E. Russian Jewry Center
117644.note: F.R.E.E. of Michigan (Chabad's organization for Soviet immigrants) began in 1990: its synagogue center under Rabbi Yosef Mishulovin opened 18 Aug 1990 (Jewish News ad, 17 Aug 1990) and F.R.E.E. is listed at 25615 Greenfield, Southfield, in Dec 1990. Its present Southfield building is later. Now at 15700 W. 10 Mile Rd., Suite 217, Southfield. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists F.R.E.E. at 15900 W. 10 Mile Rd., Suite 105 (Rabbi Yossie Mishulovin), so its move to 15700 W. 10 Mile Rd. came after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 15900 W. 10 Mile Rd., Suite 105, Southfield (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)
